Hundreds of people waited through the night – and in some cases for several days – hoping to get their hands on the “Royal Pop” timepieces, made in collaboration with luxury watchmaker Audemars Piguet.

At the Time Square location, some buyers were let into the store well before the 10 a.m. scheduled opening time – and the coveted watches were sold out in an hour.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
French police fire teargas and UK shops close for safety reasons as hundreds queue for Royal Pop timepiece

The launch of limited-edition Swatch watches descended into chaos in several European cities and New York, with French police firing teargas to restore order at a store near Paris.

Hundreds of people waited through the night from Friday into Saturday – and in some cases for several days – hoping to buy the Royal Pop timepieces, made in collaboration with the luxury watchmaker Audemars Piguet.

In France, queues of hundreds of people formed overnight in several cities and a police source said officers had fired teargas to control a 300-strong crowd outside a Swatch shop in the Paris region.

A metal shutter and two security gates were damaged in the incident. The police added the stores had underestimated the need for security.

A fight also broke out in front of a Swatch store in Milan at opening time on Saturday, according to footage broadcast by local media.

In the Netherlands, police had to intervene at a shopping centre near The Hague after hundreds flocked to the store.

The police said there had been a tense atmosphere and some quarrelling. When the store decided not to open, people had been sent home. Swatch stores in Amsterdam and Utrecht also remained closed. It is not clear when they will reopen.

On its website, the Westfield Mall of the Netherlands announced: “The introduction of Swatch in collaboration with Audemars Piguet will NOT go ahead. The store will remain closed this weekend.”

In New York, the opening of the Swatch store in Times Square saw pushing and shoving in the waiting crowd according to John McIntosh, who had been in the queue since Wednesday. “It was like a mosh pit,” he added.

Like many others, McIntosh said he had hoped to get his hands on the brightly coloured watch – sold in store for about $400 (£300) – to resell immediately at a huge mark-up.

Another buyer, who gave his name as Mac, said he had managed to get one after five days of queueing.

“It was pretty hectic … it’s nasty, but I was able to get in,” he said. “Retail for them is about $400 – I sold one just now for $4,000.”

Benny, 30, said he had decided to pay rather than to wait, and had spent $2,400 for one of the watches.

“It’s basically $2,000 over retail, but you can’t get an AP (Audemars Piguet) for less than $2,000, so I think it was a steal,” he said. “I’d rather pay a premium than come out and get it.”

Swatch was also forced to close its stores

---

[Lähde: New York Post]
Chaos erupted outside Swatch stores in NYC and across the globe as cut-throat resellers and watch enthusiasts impatiently waited for a new release – causing several locations to abruptly close amid the disastrous launch.

Hundreds of shoppers were seen swarming the stores in SoHo and Times Square Saturday morning, rounding out about a week of lengthy lines that saw the Big Apple’s sidewalks resembling tent encampments.

The frenzy is centered around the latest “Royal Pop” collaboration between Swatch and Audemars Piguet, a limited-edition, bioceramic pocket watch that merges Audemars Piguet’s iconic Royal Oak with Swatch’s vibrant POP line from the 1980s.

At the Time Square location, some buyers were let into the store well before the 10 a.m. scheduled opening time – and the coveted watches were sold out in an hour.

One particularly rowdy man was hauled off in handcuffs for his role in the ruckus.

Police were called to the scene to disperse the 600-person crowd around 11 a.m., but the disruptive man was arrested when he refused to leave, according to the NYPD.

“This is a total sh-t show,” said John McIntosh, 44. “Since Wednesday morning there was no line, just a mob scene, like a mosh pit.

“I told Swatch, ‘You have to take control of this line.’ Instead, there were a bunch of thugs since Wednesday morning setting up chairs like absentee ballots.”

At the SoHo store, the 330-person crowd reportedly got so out of hand, the location never even opened for the day.

Those waiting outside – many for days – were outraged when cops arrived and told them to get lost.

The chaos comes days after someone overdosed while waiting for the weekend product release.

The watch-fueled drama isn’t limited to NYC – or even the US – with Swatch stores across the world experiencing similarly disastrous launches.

The Swiss-based company declared on Instagram that locations in NYC, Atlanta, Houston, Los Angeles and Orlando were closed “in view of safety considerations.”

The brand issued similar statements for its stores in London, Liverpool, Manchester, Birmingham, Sheffield, Glasgow and Cardiff.

Bedlam also ensued at Dubai, Milan, Tokyo and Singapore locations, with people around the globe sharing snaps and videos of the hordes formed outside the stores.

But for those who managed to survive the relentless mobs, the launch proved successful.

Sincier Watson at the Times Square location, said he scored a black and white watch for $432 and has already sold it for $3,000.

payload.title: Swatchin Royal Pop -lanseeraus johti tungokseen Euroopassa ja New Yorkissa
payload.summary: Swatchin ja Audemars Piguet’n rajoitetun Royal Pop -kellon lanseeraus aiheutti suuria jonoja, liikkeiden sulkemisia ja järjestyshäiriöitä useissa kaupungeissa. Pariisin seudulla poliisi käytti kyynelkaasua noin 300 hengen väkijoukon hallintaan.
payload.content:
Swatchin ja luksuskellovalmistaja Audemars Piguet’n yhteisen Royal Pop -kellon lanseeraus aiheutti viikonloppuna laajoja jonoja, tungosta ja järjestyshäiriöitä useissa Euroopan kaupungeissa sekä New Yorkissa. Ranskassa poliisi käytti kyynelkaasua hallitakseen noin 300 hengen väkijoukkoa Pariisin seudulla sijaitsevan Swatch-liikkeen edustalla.

## Jonot alkoivat ennen myyntipäivää

Rajoitetun erän kellot tulivat myyntiin 16. toukokuuta, mutta osa ostajista oli odottanut niitä yön yli tai useiden päivien ajan. Lähteiden mukaan satoja ihmisiä jonotti Royal Pop -malleja, jotka on tehty Swatchin ja Audemars Piguet’n yhteistyönä.

Ranskassa satojen ihmisten jonoja muodostui yön aikana useissa kaupungeissa. Pariisin seudulla tilanne kärjistyi yhden Swatch-liikkeen ulkopuolella niin, että poliisi käytti kyynelkaasua väkijoukon hallintaan. Tapauksessa vaurioitui metallinen suojakaihdin ja kaksi turvaporttia. Poliisin mukaan liikkeet olivat aliarvioineet turvallisuusjärjestelyjen tarpeen.

Britanniassa Swatchin liikkeitä suljettiin turvallisuussyistä, kun asiakasmäärät ja jonot kasvoivat. Lanseeraukseen liittynyt väentungos ei siis rajoittunut yhteen kaupunkiin, vaan sama kaava näkyi useissa myyntipaikoissa, joissa rajoitettu saatavuus veti paikalle suuren määrän ostajia.

## New Yorkissa jonot jatkuivat päiviä

New Yorkissa satoja ihmisiä kerääntyi Swatchin liikkeiden ulkopuolelle SoHossa ja Times Squarella. Jonot olivat jatkuneet jo useita päiviä ennen lauantain myyntiä, ja osa ihmisistä leiriytyi jalkakäytäville odottamaan vuoroaan.

Times Squaren liikkeessä osa ostajista päästettiin sisään ennen kello kymmeneksi ilmoitettua avausaikaa. Kellot myytiin siellä loppuun noin tunnissa. Lanseerauksen ympärille kerääntyi sekä kelloharrastajia että jälleenmyyjiä, mikä lisäsi painetta liikkeiden edustoilla.

## Royal Pop yhdistää kaksi kellobrändiä

Royal Pop on rajoitetun erän biokeraaminen taskukello. Mallissa yhdistyvät Audemars Piguet’n Royal Oak -kellon tunnistettava muotokieli ja Swatchin 1980-luvun POP-linjaan viittaava värikäs tyyli. Lanseeraus osoitti, miten niukasti saatavilla oleva keräilytuote voi nopeasti muuttua turvallisuuskysymykseksi, jos kysyntä ylittää myymälöiden varautumisen.

Ranskassa poliisi käytti kyynelkaasua noin 300 hengen väkijoukon hallintaan Pariisin seudulla.
New Yorkin Times Squarella kellot myytiin loppuun noin tunnissa.

## New Yorkissa jonot jatkuivat päiviä

New Yorkissa satoja ihmisiä kerääntyi Swatchin liikkeiden ulkopuolelle SoHossa ja Times Squarella. Jonot olivat jatkuneet jo useita päiviä ennen lauantain myyntiä, ja osa ihmisistä leiriytyi jalkakäytäville odottamaan vuoroaan.

Times Squaren liikkeessä osa ostajista päästettiin sisään ennen kello kymmeneksi ilmoitettua avausaikaa. Kellot myytiin siellä loppuun noin tunnissa. Lanseerauksen ympärille kerääntyi sekä kelloharrastajia että jälleenmyyjiä, mikä lisäsi painetta liikkeiden edustoilla.

## Royal Pop yhdistää kaksi kellobrändiä

Royal Pop on rajoitetun erän biokeraaminen taskukello. Mallissa yhdistyvät Audemars Piguet’n Royal Oak -kellon tunnistettava muotokieli ja Swatchin 1980-luvun POP-linjaan viittaava värikäs tyyli. Lanseeraus osoitti, miten niukasti saatavilla oleva keräilytuote voi nopeasti muuttua turvallisuuskysymykseksi, jos kysyntä ylittää myymälöiden varautumisen.

French police fire teargas and UK shops close for safety reasons as hundreds queue for Royal Pop timepiece The launch of limited-edition Swatch watches descended into chaos in several European cities and New York, with French police firing teargas to restore order at a store near Paris. Hundreds of people waited through the night from Friday into Saturday – and in some cases for several days – hoping to buy the Royal Pop timepieces, made in collaboration with the luxury watchmaker Audemars Piguet. In France, queues of hundreds of people formed overnight in several cities and a police source said officers had fired teargas to control a 300-strong crowd outside a Swatch shop in the Paris region. A metal shutter and two security gates were damaged in the incident. The police added the stores had underestimated the need for security.

PARIS – The launch of limited edition Swatch watches descended into chaos on May 16 in several European cities and New York, with the French police firing tear gas to restore order at one store near Paris. Hundreds of people waited through the night – and in some cases for several days – hoping to get their hands on the “Royal Pop” timepieces, made in collaboration with luxury watchmaker Audemars Piguet.

Chaos erupted outside Swatch stores in NYC and across the globe as cut-throat resellers and watch enthusiasts impatiently waited for a new release – causing several locations to abruptly close amid the disastrous launch. Hundreds of shoppers were seen swarming the stores in SoHo and Times Square Saturday morning, rounding out about a week of lengthy lines that saw the Big Apple’s sidewalks resembling tent encampments. The frenzy is centered around the latest “Royal Pop” collaboration between Swatch and Audemars Piguet, a limited-edition, bioceramic pocket watch that merges Audemars Piguet’s iconic Royal Oak with Swatch’s vibrant POP line from the 1980s. At the Time Square location, some buyers were let into the store well before the 10 a.m. scheduled opening time – and the coveted watches were sold out in an hour.
